source_text: III. et sic raptus est athleta Christi a ministris diaboli, gratias agens deo et patri per Iesum Christum filium eius, qui eum dignum iudicavit certando diabolum superare; ductusque foras muros lapidibus caesus reddidit spiritum. Passus est autem famulus dei Maximus apud Asiam provinciam, secundo idus Maii, sub Decio imperatore et Optimo proconsule, regnante domino nostro Iesu Christo; cui est gloria in saecula saeculorum, amen.
pass_a_gloss: And in this way Christ's athlete was snatched away by the devil's attendants, while rendering thanks to God and Father through Jesus Christ his Son, who deemed him worthy by fighting to conquer the devil; and led out beyond the walls, cut down by stones, he handed back his spirit. Moreover God's slave Maximus endured suffering in the Asian province on the secundo idus of May, under Decius as emperor and Optimus as proconsul, with our Lord Jesus Christ ruling; to whom is the glory unto ages of ages, amen.
pass_b_english: And so the athlete of Christ was seized by the ministers of the devil, giving thanks to God and the Father through Jesus Christ his Son, who counted him worthy to vanquish the devil through his contest; and he was led forth beyond the walls, struck with stones, and gave up his spirit.

Now Maximus, the servant of God, suffered in the province of Asia on the second day before the Ides of May, under Decius the emperor and Optimus the proconsul, while our Lord Jesus Christ reigns, to whom is glory for ever and ever, amen.

choices.why: keeps the agonistic contest metaphor governing certando and superare, rather than generalizing to office or status
literal rendering of reddere + spiritum as yielding back life, preserving the source idiom for death
famulus marks humble service status, distinct from minister above and from later titular saint
